onboarding_tutorial.panel_title: Six steps from video to real action
onboarding_tutorial.panel_description: Review three concepts from the video, then use the same endpoint, flag input, hint reveal, and scoring controls as a real TenkaCloud problem.
onboarding_tutorial.wrong_header: Not quite. Try the other action
onboarding_tutorial.wrong_body: Read the short explanation again and choose the action this situation needs. There is no score penalty here.
onboarding_tutorial.submission_wrong_body: Check the complete value from TC{ through } and submit it again.

step_1.title: TenkaCloud uses the real cloud as the practice field
step_1.scenario: A website or app must keep running after launch. In TenkaCloud, you do not memorize an explanation—you investigate or repair a running environment.
step_1.term: A server is a computer that runs a site. Cloud is a way to rent that computer and storage. TenkaCloud turns that real environment into a safe problem.
step_1.question: What do you practice in TenkaCloud?
step_1.correct_label: Investigate and repair a running environment
step_1.correct_description: Move from “works locally” toward a service that can run in production
step_1.wrong_label: Guess a word from the description
step_1.wrong_description: Answer a knowledge quiz without touching an environment
step_1.success: TenkaCloud is not a paper quiz. You learn publishing, authentication, audit, availability, and more by working in a realistic environment.

step_2.title: Battle and Challenge: two competition formats
step_2.scenario: The video introduced two kinds of TenkaCloud problems: real-time competition and self-paced exercises.
step_2.term: In Battle, teams keep services running at the same time. In Challenge, you work at your own pace and submit a flag.
step_2.question: Which format asks you to defend a service in real time?
step_2.correct_description: Compete on uptime and recovery during the same event window
step_2.wrong_description: Investigate or repair at your own pace, then submit a flag
step_2.success: Battle is real-time; Challenge is self-paced. This first problem continues as a Challenge.

step_3.title: Choose where to run it
step_3.scenario: Choose one of the three modes from the video. Any choice moves this walkthrough forward.
step_3.term: Docker packages an app and its dependencies so a practice environment can be recreated. Local uses Docker or Codespaces, Lite uses your AWS account, and SaaS provides tenants to multiple organizations.
step_3.question: Choose one mode you want to try next.
step_3.local_description: No AWS; run supported problems with Docker or Codespaces
step_3.lite_description: Prepare TenkaCloud in your AWS account and host an event
step_3.saas_description: Serve tenants to multiple organizations; it has no recent full live verification and is not currently presented as a setup procedure
step_3.success: The mode changes where TenkaCloud runs and what setup it needs. Start with Local; use Lite to host an event.

step_4.title: Read the situation, goal, and completion condition
step_4.scenario: In a real problem, read what happened, what success means, and the first action before pressing Start.
step_4.term: The goal says what must work. The completion condition says what proves you are done. The problem ID identifies the problem when reporting an issue.
step_4.question: What should you confirm before Start?
step_4.correct_label: Situation, goal, first action, and completion condition
step_4.correct_description: Know what to investigate and what proves completion
step_4.wrong_description: Skip the problem statement and completion condition
step_4.success: The problem statement is a work order for a running environment, not an answer to memorize.

step_5.title: Start and investigate the problem environment
step_5.scenario: Start creates an isolated environment for this problem. When it reaches Running, open the displayed endpoint and find its connection code.
step_5.term: A problem environment is an isolated place for one exercise. An endpoint is the URL or address used to open it.
step_5.question: What do you do after it reaches Running?
step_5.correct_label: Open the endpoint and investigate or repair it
step_5.correct_description: Operate the running environment toward the stated goal
step_5.wrong_label: Submit a flag without opening the environment
step_5.wrong_description: Try to guess a string without solving the problem
step_5.success: Working in the running problem environment is the core TenkaCloud experience.

step_6.title: Submit the flag you found and score
step_6.scenario: Completing the goal reveals proof in the form `TC{...}`. In this walkthrough, the completion proof is shown at the practice environment endpoint.
step_6.term: TenkaCloud calls this proof a flag. The problem verifier checks it and updates the score.
step_6.question: Submit the flag found in the problem.
step_6.field_description: Submit the complete value from `TC{` through the final `}`.
step_6.success: Read the problem, start the environment, find the flag by investigating it, and submit to score. That is the real TenkaCloud loop.
